steps.title: Stream telemetry while a bearing wears
steps.say: The simulated plant runs for 20 days. Every machine sends half a second of vibration every six hours; each window is turned into features and scored as it arrives. One conveyor motor's outer bearing race is slowly failing.

steps.title: A spectral peak emerges and the anomaly score rises
steps.say: Each time a ball passes the damaged spot it rings the housing. Demodulating that ringing shows a line at the bearing's defect frequency that was not there when the machine was healthy. The health score leaves its normal range and an alert opens.

steps.title: Predict remaining useful life, with a band
steps.say: Three models give the 10th, 50th and 90th percentile of the hours left. The band is calibrated on machines the models never saw, so that it holds about 80% of the time.

steps.title: What it costs to ignore it
steps.say: Turning the prediction into money: the chance the motor fails in the next 3, 7 and 14 days, what an unplanned stop costs, and the rest of the fleet for context.

steps.title: Schedule the repairs
steps.say: An exact solver assigns each at-risk machine to a maintenance slot or leaves it, weighing failure risk against lost production, technician capacity, spare-part lead time and the life thrown away by going early. A changeover on days 5 and 6 stops the line anyway.

steps.title: Do the work, reset the health, keep the label
steps.say: The technician replaces the bearing and records what was found. That confirmation becomes a training label, the machine starts a new baseline, and three days later its health score is back in the normal range.

body.notes: Spalling on the outer race at the load zone. Bearing replaced, grease renewed.
